title: Failure injection test matrix for Private upgrade/rollback + CI automation
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Goal
Create a failure-injection test matrix for Redwood Private upgrade/rollback (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped where feasible) and automate a meaningful subset in CI.

Context
We have a new upgrade controller path in the private installer (prechecks -> backup -> staged upgrade -> validate -> commit OR rollback). We need confidence that common infra failures and expected operator mistakes do not leave the cluster in a broken partial-upgrade state.

What this ticket delivers
1) A living matrix of failure scenarios, with:
- Preconditions / environment notes (VPC vs on-prem, k8s distro/version assumptions)
- Injection method (how to trigger deterministically)
- Expected outcome (upgrade abort vs rollback, and what “healthy” means)
- Observability/triage artifacts expected (structured logs, diagnostics bundle contents, events)
- Whether the scenario is CI-automated, nightly, or manual-only

2) CI automation for a minimum set of scenarios that are stable and cheap:
- Runs on every PR that touches installer upgrade code and/or helm upgrade hooks.
- Uses ephemeral Kubernetes (kind) for basic orchestration tests.
- Uses a nightly job (real cluster runner) for the heavier tests (storage snapshot permission simulation, longer rollback windows), if we can’t keep them stable in kind.

3) Clear pass/fail gates:
- No test may pass if control plane is degraded after rollback (baseline health check required).
- Diagnostics bundle must exist on any failure path and include a precheck report + step timing summary.

Proposed matrix (initial set)
A. Disk / storage
- Disk full on node during backup (expect: backup step fails fast, upgrade does not proceed; rollback not necessary; diagnostics emitted)
- PV snapshot creation fails (permission denied / API error) (expect: upgrade aborts before touching versions; actionable error)
- Insufficient free space for offline bundle unpack (on-prem) (expect: import fails with remediation; no upgrade started)

B. Image / artifact issues
- Image pull failure for a new component version (simulate by pointing image to non-existent tag / blocking registry) (expect: upgrade halts at that step; rollback triggered if any component already advanced past rollback-safe boundary)
- Signature verification failure for offline bundle (expect: hard stop; no changes; audit log entry)

C. Control plane / API unavailability
- Control plane API unavailable during version discovery (expect: upgrade plan fails with retry guidance; no changes)
- Control plane becomes unavailable mid-upgrade (expect: installer aborts and attempts rollback if safe; ensure rollback safety checks prevent unsafe downgrade)

D. Schema / migrations
- Schema mismatch detected (forward-only migration marker present) (expect: rollback command refuses downgrade with explicit reason + next steps)
- Migration job fails (expect: upgrade aborts; rollback behavior depends on migration type; smoke tests ensure service health)

E. Kubernetes / scheduling
- Insufficient nodes/GPU capacity to roll new runtime (expect: precheck catches; otherwise upgrade step fails and exits cleanly)
- Readiness gate never becomes ready (simulate via timeout) (expect: installer stops, collects k8s events/pod logs, rollback if boundary crossed)

Injection mechanics (guidance)
- Prefer deterministic knobs: helm values that force invalid image, env var to force migration job failure, feature-flag to delay readiness.
- For disk full, simulate with an initContainer writing to an emptyDir with size constraints where possible; otherwise use a “fail backup” shim in test builds.
- For API unavailable, use a proxy sidecar / iptables in test harness (or kill deployment) and assert retry/backoff behavior is bounded.

CI strategy
- Tier 1 (per-PR): kind-based integration tests; cap total runtime <= 20 minutes.
- Tier 2 (nightly): larger matrix (storage snapshot IAM-like failures, longer rollback) on a real cluster runner.
- All tests must publish artifacts: installer logs + diagnostics tarball for debugging.

Acceptance criteria
- A test matrix document exists and is linked from ENG-2314 / the upgrade design page.
- At least 5 scenarios are fully automated in CI with deterministic failure injection and clear assertions (upgrade state + service health).
- At least 8 additional scenarios are documented as manual or nightly with exact reproduction steps.
- Tests validate rollback safety checks: rollback is blocked when migrations are forward-only; allowed otherwise.
- CI artifacts include diagnostics bundle and step timing output on failure.

Links
- Confluence: eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-upgrade-framework-overview
- Confluence: eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/rollback-policy-and-downgrade-compatibility
- Confluence: eng-sre/runbooks/private-upgrade-runbook
- Related: ENG-2321 (telemetry/diagnostics), ENG-2317 (backup primitive), ENG-2318 (rollback hooks)

Notes / risks
- kind does not model cloud snapshot APIs; treat PV snapshot failure cases as nightly/manual unless we can stub the snapshotter.
- Avoid flaky tests that depend on timing; prefer explicit readiness delays/timeouts in test builds.
- Ensure we never “test” rollback by forcibly deleting data—use the snapshot/restore path wherever possible so this reflects real operator behavior.
comments: 2025-02-13 (Leila Farouk): Drafted matrix outline + proposed CI tiers. Need clarity from Ethan on which steps are considered “rollback-safe boundaries” in v1 so assertions match policy.

2025-02-17 (Ethan Park): Rollback-safe boundaries: (1) before control plane chart upgrade starts, safe to abort without rollback; (2) once schema migration job runs, rollback depends on migration metadata (forward-only blocks); (3) once gateway/runtime roll, rollback should re-apply previous chart versions only if control plane schema is compatible. Please encode these in tests.

2025-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on artifact requirements. For any failure-path test, assert diagnostics tarball contains: precheck.json, steps.json (timings + status), kubectl get events, last 200 lines of key pods. This is critical for on-call triage.

2025-03-05 (Leila Farouk): Implemented per-PR kind harness for: image pull failure, readiness timeout, migration job failure, control plane down during version discovery, and disk-full simulation via forced backup failure hook. Working on stabilizing the control-plane-down test (race with retries).
2025-03-14 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure tests cover both `upgrade` and `rollback` CLIs (non-interactive flags). Operator UX wants CI to run with `--yes --no-prompt` to avoid hangs.

2025-03-28 (Leila Farouk): Added assertions for rollback refusal when forward-only migration marker is present (using migration metadata table). Matrix updated with injection method and expected error message snippet for Support docs.

2025-04-18 (Leila Farouk): Marking Done. Tier-1 CI runs 5 scenarios in ~17m on average. Nightly job includes snapshot-permission simulation and longer rollback window. Matrix doc linked in upgrade design and runbook draft.
